content.doc_md:
Thegit revertcommand undoes a previous commit by creating a new commit that reverses the changes.

This keeps your commit history intact and is the safest way to undo changes in a shared repository.

First, you need to find the commit you want to undo.

Usegit log --onelineto see a summary of your commit history:

Once you've found the commit you want to undo, usegit revertto create a new commit that reverses the changes:

After runninggit revert, review the changes to make sure everything is as expected:
